title: The Jnanamritasara Samhita (the Narada Pancharatra)
author: narada
attributionNote: Presented as the teaching of the sage Narada to the sages at Naimisharanya, and so broadcast as the Narada Pancharatra. It was compiled by the Vaishnava Pancharatra schools over several centuries and its first book is the one carried here.
description: The Narada Pancharatra sets out the ritual and the theology of the Pancharatra Vaishnavas: how Vishnu is to be known in his five forms, how an image is to be consecrated and worshipped, the initiations that make a worshipper, the mantras and their repetition, and the discipline of a teacher of the tradition. Its first book gathers the teaching on knowledge and on liberation into a single statement of what the sect holds.
historicalContext: The Pancharatra samhitas are the textual foundation of temple Vaishnavism, and their devotional theology underlies the Vedanta of Ramanuja, who held them to be as authoritative as the Upanishads. The Narada Pancharatra was one of the texts on the earlier acquisition register that had no verified edition; the GRETIL e-text supplies the Sanskrit of its first book.
availabilityNote: Book 1 only: the GRETIL e-text carries the first book of the samhita, 1,004 units, streamed at read time one section at a time, as the register's entry records. The remaining books are not published in this transcription and the work is not claimed as complete.
